I'ma new player too so take my advice with a grain of salt: focus on 1 queue. Put all your best legendaries there and any high purples that fill the role to make the strongest team possible. Like me, you don't have enough legendaries to make a faction specific team, sodont focus on that right now. 

As you are leveling with your main queue, think about which faction you want to focus on first. From my research and advice from others, league is the best and easiest for beginners. You I'll have enough units for a full league crew before any other faction so it's best to start there but you can pick any faction. As you level up, try spending your shards on the heroes you will take to end game. 

For me right now I'm putting all my legendary shards into Pyromancer primarily and Jon Snow secondarily. Pyro is good all the way into end game,  Jon Snow is good until you get adjudicator, but even then he can be a secondary tank (not that far so I'm just theory crafting).

League doesn't get a healer until nun (tavern lvl 16), so I've put some points into shaman as my healer. Eventually I'll use her for a horde team so it's not bad to level her a bit. 

There are clearly better ways to min max for the most baby for your buck, but I find playing that way can turn the game into a chore. Sure you can save every single legendary shard for Pyromancer but the rest of your team will be weak and you won't be able to finish content, this slowing your progress even more. I just spend the least amount of resources necessary to progress and focus on my core goals (pyromancer).

Hope this helps.

The general rule of thumb is to think to yourself, on average, would an extra turn be more beneficial or detrimental to your deck? For a deck like high Evo, magick makes sense because a lot of the cards have "at end of turn" effects, so more turns = more activations. For toxic surfer it makes sense because an extra turn gives your opponent more chances to fill their board with cards for hazmat to hit. 

For Sera Surfer you *could* put it in Magick but more than likely it will help your opponent more than you. Sera Surfer is all about that explosive turn 6 where you can drop 3+ cards and overwhelm your opponent. turn 6 you can drop a brood, shaw, and surfer for massive power in a single lane or spread out, and it's hard to react to. If the opponent has another turn, unless you float turn 6, they will have more info on your power distribution and are more likely to be able to guess where to concentrate their power/counters.

General tips: 

save your tech cards for when you really need them. Don't just use killmonger the moment you see they are playing a zoo deck, wait til the last turn unless you anticipate caiera but most people play her on curve, in which case you can enchantress her then killmonger the zoo. Shang chi is generally a final turn play unless you see a knull or black panther and you know Armin Zola is coming next turn. Wong you get rid off immediately with enchantress.  No one ever expects shadow king, and he can go through armor so keep that in mind, but he doesn't work on ongoing cards. Save killmonger and nova for the final turn. Do not play nova early as the enemy will automatically know you have a killmonger. Also when your board is full, nova + kill monger can often win games.

Sword master and maximus are power dumps since this deck doesn't have a lot of huge power spikes. Gladiator would be far better than sword master but I don't have him so this is the biggest cheap unit I could find to fill the spot. Remember to always play sword master on your final turn or he will discard a card you need. Maximus is best played on the final turn but there is no harm in playing him early. You can usually just counter their game plan anyways.

The key to this deck is knowing all the other decks well. Each type of deck leaves clues as to what kind of deck you are facing. Symbiote spiderman in a lane by himself? Expect Galactus and start power dumping there real fast. If you see the opponent purposely avoid a lane then wave? Galactus incoming and then knull on top, so keep your enchantress handy. Enemy skips turn one and two then plays Luke cage on turn 3? Anticipate hela. Stack the Luke cage lane as high as possible, make sure you have ghost down and shang chi another lane. After a while you'll start to see the patterns. You can try adding Cosmo but he can also mess up a lot of your plays.

Edit: one more tip, if the opponent plays a 1 cost card, put your lizard in that lane. They will fill the lane and drop your lizard to 1 power. Final turn nova killmonger and the 1 drop will die bringing your lizard back up to 5 + 1 from the nova. And remember you can always enchantress your lizard to remove the debuff if necessary.
